description:
Ambrook helps American family-run businesses become more profitable and resilient.
From volatile markets to climate shifts, independent operators face mounting pressure. While sustainable investments often yield the best long-term returns, they require financial clarity and capital that fragmented legacy systems can’t provide.

We are rebuilding the financial infrastructure that real economy operators rely on. By replacing paperwork with modern tools for accounting, banking, and spending, Ambrook gives owners the data they need to prove viability to lenders and the next generation. We empower the stewards of land and labor to make confident investments in their future.

We’re a Series B startup backed by Lachy Groom, Thrive Capital, Dylan Field, Thomson Reuters Ventures, Cameron Ventures, and leaders at Notion, Gusto, and Vercel. We’re looking for team members to help us untangle the intersection of American industry, climate, and the economy.

The opportunity

Ambrook’s AI Platform engineers build the shared systems that make everyone at Ambrook faster: engineers, operators, and the teams shipping AI to our customers. You’ll own two closely linked areas:

 - AI platform: the frameworks, evals, harnesses, sandboxes, tool integrations, and interfaces that let any team build, deploy, and operate agents with confidence.

 - Internal tooling: the environments, workflows, and internal products that shape how Ambrook's commercial team runs the business.

We’re working toward a world where any team can request an agent, deploy it, run evals against it, and see the results on a dashboard. Getting there means solving hard problems:

 - how agents get safe, auditable access to tools and data

 - how can we share these tools safely and securely, with auditable access

 - how can we publish custom apps or agents to share with customers

 - how we know whether a change made an agent better or worse

 - how we trace and debug what an agent did

 - how coding agents and engineers work well together in our codebase

 - how we keep cost, latency, and reliability in check as usage grows

This is engineering work, not IT. You’ll treat the people who use what you build as customers: learn how they work, iterate quickly from real feedback, and hold the quality, security, and data-integrity standards a financial product requires. Our stack is mostly TypeScript on GCP.

You’ll decide which problems are worth solving, define the patterns other teams follow, and change how the whole company works.

Within 1 month you’ll…

 - Build a working mental model of how Ambrook builds software and uses AI today: internal agent workflows, customer-facing agentic features, developer workflows and tooling, and where each breaks down.

 - Build relationships with non-engineering teams to learn where friction slows them down, and where agents could remove it.

 - Ship a meaningful improvement to production that makes it faster, safer, or easier to build software or run an agent at Ambrook.

 - Turn those conversations into a prioritized view of the biggest platform opportunities.

Within 3 months you’ll…

 - Own a platform project from discovery through rollout and adoption, such as an agent configuration interface, a shared evaluation system, a sandboxed harness for running agent loops, or a major developer workflow improvement.

 - Stand up a repeatable way to evaluate agents, so teams measure quality before and after a change instead of relying on spot checks.

 - Give agent runs real observability, including tracing, cost, latency, and failure visibility, so teams can debug and improve what they ship.

 - Set the defaults for how agents at Ambrook get context, permissions, and review, and get other teams to adopt them.

Within 6 months you’ll…

 - Own the roadmap for AI platform and developer experience, informed by internal customer needs, where the field is heading, and Ambrook’s standards for quality, security, and auditability.

 - Expand shared infrastructure that supports both internal workflows and customer-facing agentic features, including reusable evals, harnesses, sandboxes, tool integrations, and operational tooling.

 - Make it possible for a team outside engineering to request, deploy, and evaluate an agent with minimal help.

 - Show a measurable change in how Ambrook builds, such as engineering velocity, agent quality, or hours given back to operational teams.

 - Raise the bar for how Ambrook ships AI, internal tools, and customer-facing prototypes through clear design, mentorship, and production ownership.

 

About you

 - You have senior or staff-level experience building production systems that other engineers and teams depend on, and you’ve worked hands-on with LLMs in production.

 - You’ve built infrastructure for agentic systems, such as evals, agent loops, harnesses, sandboxes, or tool integrations, not only individual agents.

 - You care about developer experience and have improved how a team builds, tests, or ships software.

 - You think rigorously about measuring AI quality and understand the limits of evals, LLM-as-judge, and offline testing.

 - You treat internal teams as customers. You learn how they work, build with empathy, and measure success by adoption.

 - You can move quickly while holding the reliability and quality standards that shared infrastructure requires.

 - You’re security-minded and treat agent permissions, data access, prompt injection, auditability, and failure modes as part of ordinary engineering work.

 - Bonus: Experience with coding agents in a production codebase, tool protocols like MCP, or running untrusted code in sandboxes.

 - Bonus: Experience building financial products or systems where auditability and data integrity matter.
   
    

Our values

 - Real Talk – We create space for ourselves and others to be straightforward, vulnerable, and accountable.

 - Reach Understanding – We are driven by curiosity and empathy to learn about our customers, team, and world.

 - Be Proactively Resourceful – We are internally motivated and externally empowered to identify opportunities and solve problems.

 - Derisk Thoughtfully – We lean into the biggest risks we face as a company and put in the work to address them systematically.

 - Find the Positive-Sum – We believe in creating incentive structures that align the needs of our company, our customers, and our planet.

Benefits

 - Competitive salary

 - Health insurance

 - 401(k) with matching contribution

 - Flexible vacation time

 - Flexible work hours

 - Work-from-home/remote office stipend, or desk at Ambrook’s NYC office or Denver office

 - Wellness stipend

 - Professional development stipend
